newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei ends more than two percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei ends more than two percent higher.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index closed more than two percent higher on Wednesday, as stable currencies encouraged buying of high-tech exporters.
A rally in Wall Street stocks overnight and keen interest in Japanese telecommunication shares also supported the market.
The 225-share Nikkei average surged 461.45 points or 2.32 percent to finish at 20,351.34, just below the day's high of 20.351.64. Its June futures added 540 points to end at 20,400.

"Major high-techs that posted better-than-expected earnings results, such as NEC Corp and Fujitsu Ltd, brightened the market," said Kazuo Shiogai, deputy branch manager at ING Baring Securities (Japan) Ltd.

Brokers also said the dollar's strength against the yen supported export-oriented issues. "The dollar has been quite stable above 116.00 yen, and that boosted high-techs," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.
